title: plausible/1: plausibility of the values of an aligned feature table
description: Seven checks of the numbers a .mzfeat table shows: finite values, m/z and RT inside any real run, no negative area or height, a width for every detected peak, rows with no peak in any file, and the ppm error between the m/z of a row and its neutral mass plus adduct. Computed by crates/mzlab-feat/src/plausible.rs (same table and tolerance, same bytes). Numbers only: a flagged row is a value to look at, never a verdict on the compound.

summary.description: checks that could be made, by flag

checks.description: always in this order: non_finite, mz_range, rt_range, negative, peak_shape, empty_rows, ppm_error

flag.description: na = the check could not be made (see missing); empty_rows is a note, the others a warn

limit.description: the bounds the check reads against ([min, max] or the single limit), empty when it has none

rows.description: table ids of the first rows flagged, ascending

missing.description: why the check was not made: unit resolution, or no identity columns
